name: Electric Scooter
description: A light two- or three-wheeled device with handlebars, ridden standing or seated and powered by an electric motor and human power, that can't exceed 20 mph and weighs 110 pounds or less; it has no motor wattage limit. Treated much like a bicycle rather than a motor vehicle.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and handlebars, designed to be ridden standing or seated, and powered by an electric motor and human power; not an electric bicycle or a one-wheeled vehicle
Its top speed on a paved level surface, with or without human propulsion, is no more than 20 mph
Weighs no more than 110 pounds (100 pounds before October 1, 2026)
restrictions.citation: Connecticut General Statutes §14-1(32), as amended by Public Act 26-24

restrictions.rule: Not a motor vehicle or a motor-driven cycle, so needs no driver's license or state registration; towns may require annual licensing and register sales by ordinance
Has the rights and duties of a vehicle driver on the road, riding near the right edge when slower than traffic, and may use bicycle lanes and cycle tracks
Riders 17 and under should wear a bicycle helmet on highways and in parks, though not wearing one isn't an offense; rental businesses must supply one to riders that age
On a sidewalk or crosswalk it yields to pedestrians and sounds a warning before passing, and a town may ban riding there
May be parked on a sidewalk where it doesn't block pedestrians, unless a local ordinance forbids it
Needs a white front lamp at night, visible from 500 feet, and a rear reflector
Carries a passenger only if built to carry one
